# Agent SDK OpenTelemetry

Customers configure export with standard `OTEL_*` environment variables
and secrets. There is no instrumentation file and no `defineOtel`.
`ctx.host.otel` is deprecated. Use `metrics.getMeter` and
`trace.getTracer`. A span during a turn gets `cursor.conversation.id`
from the active context. A metric you record does not. Call
`currentConversationId` from `@grok/agent-sdk/otel` and set it yourself.

To tag one turn, call `ctx.telemetry` from a tool. Trace tags land
on spans started in that turn, including spans Agent SDK starts. Metric
tags land on `cursor.token.usage`. Log tags land on log records Agent SDK
emits. The tags stay in the process and are not written on the
`baggage` header. Each distinct metric value is its own series.

```ts
async execute({ key }, ctx) {
  ctx.telemetry.setTraceAttributes({ "work.item": key });
  ctx.telemetry.setMetricAttributes({ "work.item": key });
  ctx.telemetry.setLogAttributes({ "work.item": key });
}
```

`telemetry.setTraceAttributes` and the other global methods read the
active context. Outside a turn they do nothing.

With export off, tags apply for the rest of that turn only.
A later turn does not see them. Agent SDK does not export those tags.

If a context manager is already registered, Agent SDK writes a warning and
does not replace it. Load Agent SDK before another SDK registers a context
manager, or the turn store does not stay on the active context.

`setMetricAttributes` rejects keys Agent SDK writes on metrics, including
`cursor.token.type`, `agent_sdk.channel`, `cursor.tool.name`, and
`agent_sdk.turn_status`. The call throws and does not replace the
runtime value. Trace and log keys are accepted. Do not put a secret,
an email, or a raw user id in a metric value.

Guide: `docs/guides/opentelemetry.md`.

```bash
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otel.example.com
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS="Authorization=Bearer $OTEL_TOKEN"
export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=incident-agent
```

Agent SDK installs trace, metric, and log providers before `bot/agent.ts`.
A module-scope `trace.getTracer()`, `metrics.getMeter()`, or
`logs.getLogger()` binds to those providers. Exporters attach when
secrets load. With no `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` endpoint, export stays
off. Outbound fetch does not gain a `traceparent` header, and the
session collector stays disabled.

Metrics use delta temporality by default. For Grafana Cloud, set
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE=cumulative`.

Do not pass `otel` to `serve`. Do not add `bot/otel.ts`.
Read the guide section "Migrating from serve({ otel })".

Hosted agents:

- Put the same variables in `agent-sdk secret set`, and add the collector
  host to `hosting.egressDomains`.
- Header values are URL-encoded (`Authorization=Basic%20...`).
- A new header or URL from `agent-sdk secret set` applies on the next export.

Not supported yet: custom span processors, samplers, views, your own
SDK, and library auto-instrumentation. A span that ends before the
exporters attach is still exported. `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` and
`OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL` are read when the provider is built.
